references.text: The meat, skin, and dung of the sin offering were to be burned outside the camp, just as with the red heifer that is completely burned.
The bull for the sin offering was to be burned outside the camp along with its skin, meat, and dung, following the same principle as the red heifer.
The bull for the sin offering was to be burned outside the camp, parallel to the burning of the red heifer.
The bull, including its skin, meat, and dung, was burned with fire outside the camp, the same practice used for the red heifer.
The meat and skin of the sin offering were burned with fire outside the camp.
On the Day of Atonement, the bull and goat for the sin offering were to be burned outside the camp, including their skin, meat, and dung.
Hebrews refers to animals whose blood is brought into the sanctuary but whose bodies are burned outside the camp, linking this to Jesus' suffering outside the city gate.
